title.en: Volume 225 Biographies 12: E Yi Dou, Fei Yingdong son: Suo Hai, Sun :wohei, He Heli son: Duo Ji Li, He Shuotu, Dou Lei An Fei Yang Gu, Hu Er Han
title.raw: 卷225 列傳十二 额亦都 费英东子：索海 孙:倭黑 何和礼子：多积礼 和硕图 都类安费扬古 扈尔汉

sentences.zh: 額亦都費英東子索海孫倭黑何和禮子多積禮和碩圖都類

translations.literal: E Yidu; Fei Yingdong; son Suo Hai; grandson Wohei; He Heli; son Duo Jili, Heshuotu, and Dulei.
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu; Fei Yingdong; his son Suo Hai; his grandson Wohei; He Heli; his sons Duo Jili and Heshuotu; and Dulei.

sentences.zh: 安費揚古扈爾漢

translations.literal: Anfiyanggu; Hu Erhan.
translations.idiomatic: Anfiyanggu; Hu Erhan.

sentences.zh: 額亦都，鈕祜祿氏，世居長白山。

translations.literal: E Yidu was of the Niohuru clan and for generations his family dwelt on Changbai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu belonged to the Niohuru clan; his family had lived on Changbai Mountain for generations.

sentences.zh: 以資雄鄉里。

translations.literal: With his wealth he was the strongest man in the district.
translations.idiomatic: His family wealth made him the most formidable man in the locality.

sentences.zh: 祖阿陵阿拜顏，移居英崿峪。

translations.literal: His grandfather Aringa Baibayan moved the household to Ying'eyu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Aringa Baibayan relocated the clan to Ying'eyu.

sentences.zh: 父都陵阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: His father was Dulungga Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Dulungga Baturu.

sentences.zh: 歲壬戌，額亦都生。

translations.literal: In the year renxu, E Yidu was born.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the renxu year.

sentences.zh: 幼時，父母為仇家所殺，匿鄰村以免。

translations.literal: In childhood his parents were killed by an enemy family; he hid in a neighboring village to escape.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child, his parents were murdered by a feuding clan; he took refuge in a neighboring village.

sentences.zh: 年十三，手刃其仇。

translations.literal: At thirteen he slew his enemy with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of thirteen he killed the murderer himself.

sentences.zh: 有姑嫁嘉木瑚寨長穆通阿，往依焉。

translations.literal: He had an aunt married to Mutongga, chief of the Jiamuhu stockade, and went to rely on them.
translations.idiomatic: An aunt of his was married to Mutongga, headman of the Jiamuhu stockade, and he went to live under that roof.

sentences.zh: 穆通阿子哈思護，長額亦都二歲，相得甚懽。

translations.literal: Mutongga's son Hasihu was two years older than E Yidu; the two became very close.
translations.idiomatic: Mutongga's son Hasihu was two years E Yidu's senior, and the two became inseparable companions.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，庚辰，太祖行經嘉木瑚寨，宿穆通阿家。

translations.literal: After several years, in the year gengchen, the Taizu passed through the Jiamuhu stockade and lodged at Mutongga's home.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later, in the gengchen year, the Taizu was traveling through Jiamuhu and spent the night at Mutongga's house.

sentences.zh: 額亦都與太祖語，心知非常人，遂請從，其姑止之，額亦都曰：「大丈夫生世間，能以碌碌終乎？

translations.literal: E Yidu spoke with the Taizu, knew in his heart that this was no ordinary man, and asked to follow him. His aunt tried to stop him. E Yidu said, "Can a man born into this world end in mere mediocrity?
translations.idiomatic: Speaking with the Taizu, E Yidu sensed at once that he was no ordinary man and asked to join him. His aunt objected, but E Yidu said, "Can a man who enters this world expect to end his days in obscurity?

sentences.zh: 此行任所之，誓不貽姑憂。」

translations.literal: On this journey I shall go wherever fate leads; I swear I will bring no grief to my aunt."
translations.idiomatic: Wherever this road takes me, I swear I will not be the cause of sorrow to you, Aunt."

sentences.zh: 翌日，遂從太祖行。

translations.literal: The next day he set out with the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he left with the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 是歲太祖年二十二，額亦都年十九。

translations.literal: That year the Taizu was twenty-two and E Yidu nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu was twenty-two that year; E Yidu was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 太祖為族人所惎，數見侵侮，矢及於戶，額亦都護左右，卒弭其難。

translations.literal: The Taizu was envied by clansmen and repeatedly insulted; arrows reached his door. E Yidu guarded him on either side and at last quelled the trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen bore the Taizu ill will and harassed him again and again—arrows even struck his doorway. E Yidu stood guard at his side until the danger finally passed.

sentences.zh: 居三年，歲癸未，太祖起兵，額亦都從，討尼堪外蘭，攻圖倫城，先登；

translations.literal: After three years, in the year guiwei, the Taizu raised his army. E Yidu followed him, campaigning against Nikhan Wailan, attacking Tulun city and being first to scale the wall;
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, in the guiwei year, the Taizu took up arms. E Yidu marched with him against Nikhan Wailan, stormed Tulun, and was the first man over the wall;

sentences.zh: 攻色克濟城，掩敵無備，取之，獲其牛馬、甲士；

translations.literal: he attacked Sekiji city, took the enemy unawares, captured it, and seized cattle, horses, and armored men;
translations.idiomatic: he struck Sekiji before the enemy was ready, took the town, and seized its cattle, horses, and armored fighters;

sentences.zh: 又別將兵攻舒勒克布佔，克其城。

translations.literal: he also led troops separately to attack Shulekebuzhan and captured that city.
translations.idiomatic: and he led a separate detachment against Shulekebuzhan and reduced that city as well.

sentences.zh: 額亦都驍果善戰，所向克捷，太祖知其能，日見信任。

translations.literal: E Yidu was fierce and skilled in battle; wherever he went victory followed. The Taizu knew his ability and daily placed more trust in him.
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu was bold and masterful in war; his campaigns were invariably successful. Recognizing his talent, the Taizu came to rely on him more with each passing day.

sentences.zh: 歲丁亥八月，令將兵取巴爾達城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the year dinghai he was ordered to lead troops to take Bardai city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the dinghai year he was ordered to take Bardai with an army.

sentences.zh: 至渾河，秋水方至，不能涉，以繩約軍士，魚貫而渡，夜薄其城，率驍卒先登，城兵驚起拒，跨堞而戰，飛矢貫股著於堞，揮刀斷矢，戰益力，被五十餘創，不退，卒拔其城。

translations.literal: At the Hun River the autumn flood had just risen and they could not ford it. He bound the soldiers with ropes and had them cross in single file. At night they pressed the city; leading crack troops he was first to climb the wall. The garrison sprang up to resist. Fighting astride the parapet, a flying arrow pierced his thigh and pinned it to the battlement; he swung his blade and cut the shaft, fought all the harder, suffered more than fifty wounds, would not retreat, and at last stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hun River the autumn waters were high and the army could not cross. He roped the men together and had them ford in single file. That night they closed on the city; at the head of picked warriors he was first over the wall. The defenders rushed to meet him. Fighting from the parapet, a stray arrow drove through his thigh and pinned him to the merlon; he hacked off the shaft with his sword, fought on with redoubled fury, took more than fifty wounds, and would not yield until the city fell.

sentences.zh: 師還，太祖迎於郊，燕勞，其所俘獲悉畀之，號為「巴圖魯」。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Taizu met him in the suburbs, feasted him, and gave him all the captives and booty, styling him "Baturu."
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the Taizu welcomed him outside the walls, held a feast in his honor, handed over the entire haul of prisoners and spoils, and gave him the title Baturu, "the Brave."

sentences.zh: 薩克察來攻，額亦都率數卒出禦，為所敗；

translations.literal: Sakcha came to attack; E Yidu led a few soldiers out to meet him and was defeated;
translations.idiomatic: When Sakcha attacked, E Yidu went out with only a handful of men and was driven back;

sentences.zh: 夜入其城，進攻克尼瑪蘭、章家二城，索爾瑚寨。

translations.literal: that night he entered their city, advanced, and captured the two cities of Nikmalan and Zhangjia and the Suoerhu stockade.
translations.idiomatic: but that night he stole into the enemy town, pressed forward, and took Nikmalan, Zhangjia, and the Suoerhu stockade.

sentences.zh: 師還，太祖迎勞如初。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Taizu welcomed and rewarded him as before.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the Taizu received and honored him just as he had after his first triumph.

sentences.zh: 界籓有科甚者，以勇聞，盜九馬以遁，額亦都單騎追斬之，盡返所盜馬。

translations.literal: On the frontier there was a man of unusual stature famed for courage who stole nine horses and fled. E Yidu pursued alone on horseback, cut him down, and recovered every stolen horse.
translations.idiomatic: A man of extraordinary build on the border, renowned for valor, stole nine horses and fled. E Yidu rode after him alone, killed him, and brought back every horse.

sentences.zh: 嘉木瑚人貝揮巴顏謀叛附哈達，太祖命額亦都討之，誅其父子五人以徇。

translations.literal: Beihuibayan of Jiamuhu plotted rebellion to join Hada. The Taizu ordered E Yidu to punish him; he executed father and sons, five men in all, as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Beihuibayan of Jiamuhu plotted to rebel and join Hada. The Taizu sent E Yidu against him; he put five men of that house to death, father and sons together, as an example to others.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳九月，葉赫等九部合師來侵，攻我黑濟格城，太祖親御之，陣於古勒山。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the year guisi, Yehe and eight other tribes united their armies to invade and attacked our Heijige city. The Taizu commanded in person and drew up battle at Gule Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the guisi year, Yehe and eight other tribes joined forces to invade and assaulted Heijige. The Taizu took the field in person and formed his line at Gule Mountain.

sentences.zh: 令額來犯，奮擊，殪九人，敵卻，我師乘之，擒葉赫貝勒布寨。

translations.literal: He ordered E Yidu to challenge the enemy with a hundred horsemen. When the foe came in full force he charged fiercely, killed nine men, and the enemy fell back; our army pressed the pursuit and captured the Yehe beile Buzhai.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered E Yidu forward with a hundred horsemen to offer battle. When the enemy came on in full strength he struck hard, killed nine men, and forced them back; our troops followed up and took the Yehe beile Buzhai prisoner.

sentences.zh: 九部師？

translations.literal: The armies of the nine tribes were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies of the nine tribes broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 亦都以百騎挑戰，敵悉皆潰，遂乘勝略諾賽寨及兆佳村。

translations.literal: E Yidu again challenged with a hundred horsemen; the enemy all scattered. Taking advantage of victory he overran the Nuosai stockade and Zhaojia village.
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu again rode out with a hundred horsemen; the enemy lines collapsed entirely. Pressing the advantage, he overran the Nuosai stockade and Zhaojia village.

sentences.zh: 有齊法罕者，戰沒，額亦都直入敵陣，以其屍還。

translations.literal: A man named Qifahan fell in battle; E Yidu plunged straight into the enemy ranks and brought back his body.
translations.idiomatic: When Qifahan was killed in the fighting, E Yidu charged deep into the enemy formation and recovered his corpse.

sentences.zh: 訥殷路守佛多和山自固。

translations.literal: The Neyinlu tribe held Mount Foduohe and stood firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Neyinlu people held Mount Foduohe and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 太祖命額亦都？

translations.literal: The Taizu ordered E Yidu, together with Gagai and Anfiyanggu, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu ordered E Yidu, together with Gagai and Anfiyanggu, to move against them.

sentences.zh: 者，九部之一也，其長搜穩塞克什，既敗歸，复聚七寨之偕噶蓋、安費揚古，以兵千人圍其寨，克之，斬搜穩塞克什，太祖以所乘馬賜之。

translations.literal: The Neyinlu were one of the nine tribes. Their chief Suwensakexi, after defeat, had returned and gathered the people of seven stockades to hold Mount Foduohe. With a thousand men they besieged the stockade, took it, and beheaded Suwensakexi. The Taizu gave E Yidu the horse on which he himself had ridden.
translations.idiomatic: The Neyinlu were one of the nine allied tribes. Their chief Suwensakexi, beaten once, had rallied the people of seven stockades to defend Mount Foduohe. E Yidu invested the place with a thousand men, stormed it, and cut off Suwensakexi's head. The Taizu rewarded him with his own mount.

sentences.zh: 歲己亥秋，從征哈達，滅之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the year jihai he followed the campaign against Hada and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the jihai year he joined the expedition against Hada and helped bring about its destruction.

sentences.zh: 歲丁未五月，從貝勒巴雅喇等伐東海渥集部，取赫席黑、俄漠和蘇魯、佛訥赫拖克索等三路，俘二千人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the year dingwei he followed the beile Bayara and others to campaign against the Eastern Sea Woji tribe, taking the three routes of Hexihei, Emohesulu, and Fonehetuokesuo, and capturing two thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the dingwei year he marched with Bayara and other beiles against the Eastern Sea Woji, securing the Hexihei, Emohesulu, and Fonehetuokesuo routes and taking two thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 九月，從征輝發，滅之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed the expedition against Huifa and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he joined the campaign against Huifa and helped destroy that state.

sentences.zh: 歲庚戌十一月，太祖命將兵千，撫渥集部那木都魯、綏分、寧古塔、尼瑪察四路，降其長康古禮等十九人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the year gengxu the Taizu ordered him to lead a thousand men to pacify the four routes of Namudulu, Suifen, Ningguta, and Nimacha in the Woji tribe; he received the submission of nineteen chiefs including Kanguli.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the gengxu year the Taizu sent him with a thousand men to bring the Namudulu, Suifen, Ningguta, and Nimacha routes of the Woji under control; nineteen chiefs, including Kanguli, submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 旋乘勝取雅攬路，俘萬人。

translations.literal: He then pressed his advantage to take the Yalan route and captured ten thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately followed up by taking the Yalan route and bringing away ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥，太祖命偕何和禮、扈爾漢將兵二千伐渥集部虎爾哈路，圍札庫塔城三日，招之不下，遂攻克其城，斬千級，俘二千人。

translations.literal: In the year xinhai the Taizu ordered him, together with He Heli and Hu Erhan, to lead two thousand men against the Hu'erha route of the Woji tribe. They invested Zhakuta city for three days; summons to surrender failed, so they stormed the city, slew a thousand, and took two thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinhai year the Taizu sent him with He Heli and Hu Erhan and two thousand troops against the Hu'erha route of the Woji. They besieged Zhakuta for three days; when the defenders would not yield, they carried the place by assault, killed a thousand men, and took two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 環近各路悉降，令其長土勒伸、額勒伸護其民五百戶以還。

translations.literal: All neighboring routes submitted. He ordered the chiefs Tuleshen and Eleshen to escort five hundred households back.
translations.idiomatic: Every nearby route then submitted. He left the chiefs Tuleshen and Eleshen to escort five hundred households home under guard.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，從征烏拉，滅之。

translations.literal: In the year guichou he followed the expedition against Ula and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year he joined the campaign against Ula and helped destroy it.

sentences.zh: 歲乙卯，定旗制，額亦都隸滿洲鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: In the year yimao the banner system was fixed; E Yidu was enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year the Eight Banners were established; E Yidu was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命建元，置五大臣，以命額亦都，國語謂之「達拉哈轄」。

translations.literal: When the Tianming reign was inaugurated, the Five Great Ministers were appointed; E Yidu was among them, called in the national language "Dalahaqi."
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianming era began, the Five Great Ministers were created and E Yidu was named to their number—the court tongue called the office Dalahaqi.

sentences.zh: 二年，命偕安費揚古攻明馬根單、花豹衝、三岔兒諸堡，皆克之。

translations.literal: In the second year he was ordered with Anfiyanggu to attack the Ming forts of Magendan, Huabaochong, and Sancha'er; all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he and Anfiyanggu were ordered against the Ming strongholds of Magendan, Huabaochong, and Sancha'er; all fell.

sentences.zh: 四年，明經略楊鎬大舉來侵，總兵杜松軍自撫順入。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Ming grand coordinator Yang Hao came in force. The commander Du Song entered from Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Ming grand coordinator Yang Hao launched a major invasion. The commander Du Song advanced from Fushun.

sentences.zh: 三月甲申朔，諸貝勒帥師出禦。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, jiashen, the beiles led the army out to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month, jiashen, the beiles marched out to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 日過午，師至太蘭岡，大貝勒代善以太祖未至，議駐軍以俟。

translations.literal: Past noon the army reached Tailangang. The senior beile Daishan, because the Taizu had not yet arrived, proposed halting to wait.
translations.idiomatic: By afternoon the force had reached Tailangang. Daishan, the senior beile, urged a halt because the Taizu had not yet come up.

sentences.zh: 太宗時號四貝勒，謂：「界籓有我築城夫役，宜急護之！

translations.literal: The Fourth Beile, later known as the Taizong, said, "At Jiefan our men building the fort are there—we must hurry to protect them!
translations.idiomatic: The Fourth Beile—later the Taizong—said, "Our laborers are building the fort at Jiefan; we must reach them at once!

sentences.zh: 何為次，且示弱？」

translations.literal: Why hold back and show weakness?"
translations.idiomatic: Why delay and look timid?"

sentences.zh: 額亦都大言曰：「四貝勒之言是也！」

translations.literal: E Yidu spoke up loudly: "The Fourth Beile is right!"
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu cried out, "The Fourth Beile speaks the truth!"

sentences.zh: 師遂進。

translations.literal: The army then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The column moved forward.

sentences.zh: 師至界籓，築城夫役騰躍下山赴戰，太祖亦至，指揮夾擊，松軍遂覆，還破馬林于尚間崖、劉綎於阿布達里岡，額亦都並為軍鋒。

translations.literal: When the army reached Jiefan, the fort builders leapt down the hill to join the fight. The Taizu also arrived and directed a pincer attack; Song's army was destroyed. They went on to defeat Ma Lin at Shangjianya and Liu Ting at Abudali Gang; E Yidu served throughout as the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiefan the builders rushed downhill to fight. The Taizu came up as well and ordered a double envelopment; Du Song's force was annihilated. They next broke Ma Lin at Shangjianya and Liu Ting at Abudali Gang, with E Yidu always in the van.

sentences.zh: 太祖有所征討，額亦都皆在行間，未嘗挫衂。

translations.literal: Whenever the Taizu undertook a campaign, E Yidu was in the ranks and never met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In every campaign the Taizu undertook, E Yidu marched with him and never knew a reverse.

sentences.zh: 每克敵受賜，輙散給將士之有功者，不以自私，太祖厚遇之，始妻以族妹，後以和碩公主降焉。

translations.literal: Whenever he received spoils after victory he at once distributed them to officers and men who had earned merit, never keeping them for himself. The Taizu treated him with exceptional favor: first he gave him a clanswoman in marriage, later a princess of the blood.
translations.idiomatic: Prize after prize he handed straight to the men who had fought well, never hoarding for himself. The Taizu favored him richly—first with a clanswoman as wife, later with an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 額亦都次子達啟，少材武，太祖育於宮中，長使尚皇女。

translations.literal: Daqi, E Yidu's second son, was gifted in youth with martial talent. The Taizu reared him in the palace and when he grew up had him betrothed to an imperial daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi, the second son of E Yidu, showed martial promise early. The Taizu raised him in the palace and, when he came of age, matched him to a princess.

sentences.zh: 達啟怙寵而驕，遇諸皇子無皆愕。

translations.literal: Daqi, relying on favor, grew arrogant; when he met the princes he showed no courtesy, and all were startled.
translations.idiomatic: Spoiled by privilege, Daqi grew insolent; in the presence of the princes he behaved without proper respect, to everyone's dismay.

sentences.zh: 額亦都抽刃而言？

translations.literal: E Yidu drew his blade and said, "If you again treat the princes without courtesy, this blade will take your head!
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu drew his sword and declared, "Show the princes disrespect again and this blade will answer for it!

sentences.zh: 禮，額亦都患之。

translations.literal: Daqi then learned some measure of propriety, yet E Yidu still worried over him.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi thereafter observed a little more decorum, but his father remained uneasy.

sentences.zh: 一日，集諸子宴別墅，酒行，忽起，命執達啟，曰：「天下安有父殺子者？

translations.literal: One day he gathered his sons for a feast at a villa. As the wine went round he suddenly rose and ordered Daqi seized, saying, "Under heaven is there a father who kills his own son?
translations.idiomatic: One day he feasted his sons at a country house. Wine had barely circulated when he rose abruptly and had Daqi seized. "Is there anywhere under heaven a father who slays his own son?" he said.

sentences.zh: 顧此子傲慢，及今不治，他日必負國敗門戶，不從者血此刃！」

translations.literal: Yet this boy is arrogant; if he is not corrected now, one day he will betray the state and ruin our house. Whoever refuses—let this blade drink his blood!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the boy is insufferably proud. Leave him unchecked and he will one day betray the realm and destroy our line. Whoever will not obey—this sword will find him!"

sentences.zh: 乃懼，引達啟入室，以被覆殺之。

translations.literal: They were terrified; they led Daqi into a room and smothered him beneath a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were terrified; they took Daqi inside and suffocated him under a quilt.

sentences.zh: 額亦都詣太祖謝，太祖驚惋久之，乃嗟嘆，謂額亦都為？

translations.literal: E Yidu went to the Taizu to apologize. The Taizu was long astonished and grieved, then sighed and said that E Yidu's concern for the state
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu went to the Taizu to report what he had done. The sovereign was stunned and grieved for a long while, then sighed and said that E Yidu's care for the realm

sentences.zh: 國深慮，不可及也。

translations.literal: was profound beyond comparison.
translations.idiomatic: ran deeper than any man's and could not be matched.

sentences.zh: 累官至左翼總兵官、一等大臣，給以百人廩食，食三世。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to commander-in-chief of the Left Wing and a first-rank great minister, with provision for a hundred men for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander-in-chief of the Left Wing and first-rank great minister, with rations for a hundred retainers heritable for three generations.

sentences.zh: 分所部為世管牛錄三，分隸鑲黃、正白二旗。

translations.literal: His following was divided into three hereditary niru, assigned to the Bordered Yellow and Plain White Banners.
translations.idiomatic: His command was split into three hereditary niru, apportioned between the Bordered Yellow and Plain White Banners.

sentences.zh: 六年，克遼陽，賜第一區。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liaoyang was taken and he was granted a first-class residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when Liaoyang fell, he received a premier dwelling in the city.

sentences.zh: 六月，卒，年六十，太祖臨哭者三。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he died at the age of sixty; the Taizu came three times to mourn at his bier.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month at sixty; the Taizu visited his coffin three times to weep.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，追封弘毅公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke Hongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancong he was posthumously created Duke Hongyi.

sentences.zh: 崇德初，配享太廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongde he was given a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongde reign he was granted a share in sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，世祖命立碑旌功，親為製文，詳著其戰閥，以為「忠勇忘身，有始有卒，開拓疆土，厥積懋焉」。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi the Shizu ordered a stele erected to proclaim his merit; he composed the text himself, setting forth his battles in detail, praising him as "loyal and brave, forgetting self, beginning and ending true, opening the frontier—his achievement abundant."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi the Shizu ordered a monument raised to his merit and wrote the inscription himself, recounting his campaigns in full and calling him "loyal and valiant, heedless of self, steadfast from first to last, who widened the realm—his deeds weighty indeed."

sentences.zh: 額亦都子十六人，其知名者，徹爾格、圖爾格、伊爾登、超哈爾、遏必隆，皆自有傳。

translations.literal: E Yidu had sixteen sons; those of note—Cheerge, Tuerge, Yierdeng, Chaohaer, and Ebilun—each have their own biography.
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu left sixteen sons. The best known—Cheerge, Tuerge, Yierdeng, Chaohaer, and Ebilun—each has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 四子韓代，五子阿達海，及阿達海之子阿哈尼堪，並以從征戰死。

translations.literal: The fourth son Handai, the fifth son Adahai, and Adahai's son Ahanikan all died in battle on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son Handai, the fifth son Adahai, and Adahai's son Ahanikan all fell on campaign.

sentences.zh: 七子謨海，蚤歲從軍，屢立戰功，仕至都統，亦戰死。

translations.literal: The seventh son Mohai entered the army young, won repeated battle honors, rose to dutong, and also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh son Mohai took the field in his youth, won distinction again and again, rose to dutong, and likewise died in action.

sentences.zh: 十五子索渾，從太宗戰伐有功，授世管牛錄額真，累遷至議政大臣。

translations.literal: The fifteenth son Suohun followed the Taizong on campaign with merit, was made hereditary niru daikan, and rose to councilor of state.
translations.idiomatic: The fifteenth son Suohun served the Taizong in war with credit, received a hereditary niru command, and eventually became a grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 額亦都初授一等總兵官，康熙間改襲一等精奇尼哈番，乾隆元年改一等子。

translations.literal: E Yidu was first granted the first-rank commander-in-chief; under Kangxi the succession became the first-rank jingqiniha fan; in the first year of Qianlong it became a first-rank zi.
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu was first ennobled as first-rank commander-in-chief; under Kangxi the line inherited a first-rank jingqiniha fan; in Qianlong's first year it became a first-rank zi.

sentences.zh: 圖爾格別封公爵，以其從孫阿里袞及阿里袞子豐升額父子相繼有功，進一等果毅繼勇公。

translations.literal: Tuerge received a separate ducal title; his collateral descendant Arigun and Arigun's son Fengsheng'e, father and son succeeding in merit, were advanced to first-rank Guoyi Jiyong Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Tuerge was enfeoffed separately as duke; his collateral descendant Arigun and Arigun's son Fengsheng'e, each adding to the family's merit, were raised to first-rank Guoyi Jiyong Gong.

sentences.zh: 高宗諭：「額亦都後已進一等公，其初封子爵仍紹封如故。」

translations.literal: The Gaozong instructed: "E Yidu's line has already been advanced to first-rank duke; the original enfeoffment as zi should still be inherited as before."
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong directed: "E Yidu's descendants have already been raised to first-rank duke, yet the original zi title shall continue to pass down the line as before."

sentences.zh: 費英東，瓜爾佳氏，蘇完部人。

translations.literal: Fei Yingdong was of the Guwalgiya clan, a man of the Suwan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yingdong belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and came from the Suwan tribe.

sentences.zh: 父索爾果，為部長。

translations.literal: His father Suoerguo was tribal chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Suoerguo was chief of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵之六年，歲戊子，索爾果率所部五百戶來歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year after the Taizu raised his army, the year wuzi, Suoerguo led five hundred households of his tribe to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Taizu's uprising, the wuzi year, Suoerguo brought five hundred households of his people to submit.

sentences.zh: 費英東時年​​二十有五，善射，引強弓十餘石。

translations.literal: Fei Yingdong was then twenty-five, skilled in archery, and could draw a bow of more than ten piculs' strength.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yingdong was twenty-five at the time, a master archer who could bend a bow rated at more than ten piculs.

sentences.zh: 忠直敢言，太祖使佐理政事，授一等大臣，以皇長子台吉褚英女妻焉。

translations.literal: Loyal, upright, and outspoken, the Taizu had him assist in governing affairs, granted him the rank of first-rank great minister, and gave him the eldest imperial son Taiji Cuying's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Frank and fearless in counsel, he was set to help govern; the Taizu made him a first-rank great minister and gave him the eldest imperial son Taiji Cuying's daughter as wife.

sentences.zh: 兌沁巴顏者，費英東女兄之夫也，有逆謀，費英東擒而誅之。

translations.literal: Duiqinbayan, husband of Fei Yingdong's elder sister by marriage, plotted rebellion; Fei Yingdong seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Duiqinbayan, who had married Fei Yingdong's elder sister, plotted treason; Fei Yingdong arrested him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 旋授扎爾固齊，扎爾固齊職聽訟治民。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Zargaci; the office of Zargaci was to hear lawsuits and govern the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Zargaci—an office charged with hearing suits and governing the people.

sentences.zh: 以歸。

translations.literal: Those who submitted returned.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had submitted were sent home.

sentences.zh: 歲戊戌正月，太祖？

translations.literal: In the first month of the year wuxu the Taizu ordered
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the wuxu year the Taizu ordered

sentences.zh: 太祖命費英東伐瓦爾喀部，取噶嘉路，殺其酋阿球，降其命費英東從台吉褚英、巴雅喇，伐瓦爾喀部安褚拉庫路，將兵千，克屯寨二十餘，收所屬村落。

translations.literal: the Taizu ordered Fei Yingdong to campaign against the Warka tribe, take the Gajia route, kill the chief Aqiu, and receive their submission; he ordered Fei Yingdong with Taiji Cuying and Bayara against the Antulaku route of the Warka with a thousand men, took more than twenty stockaded villages, and received all dependent hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yingdong against the Warka: he took the Gajia route, killed the chief Aqiu, and brought the people in; then, with Taiji Cuying and Bayara, he marched on the Antulaku route with a thousand men, reduced more than twenty fortified villages, and brought every dependent settlement under control.

sentences.zh: 歲己亥秋九月，哈達、葉赫二部構兵，哈達貝勒孟格布祿乞援於太祖，太祖命費英東及噶蓋將兵二千戍哈達；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in the year jihai, Hada and Yehe were at war. The Hada beile Menggebulu begged aid from the Taizu; the Taizu ordered Fei Yingdong and Gagai with two thousand men to garrison Hada;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the jihai year Hada and Yehe went to war. The Hada beile Menggebulu begged the Taizu for help; the Taizu sent Fei Yingdong and Gagai with two thousand men to hold Hada;

sentences.zh: 既而貳於明，費英東等以其謀聞，哈達以是亡。

translations.literal: later they turned to Ming; Fei Yingdong and the others reported their plot, and Hada perished for it.
translations.idiomatic: but Hada soon leaned toward the Ming. Fei Yingdong reported the treachery, and Hada was destroyed on that account.

sentences.zh: 歲丁未春正月，瓦爾喀部蜚悠城長策穆特黑請徙所部屬太祖，太祖命費英東從貝勒舒爾哈齊等將兵三千以往，收環城居民五百戶，分兵三百授扈爾漢，使護之先行。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the year dingwei, Cemutehei, chief of Feiyoucheng in the Warka tribe, asked to move his people under the Taizu. The Taizu ordered Fei Yingdong with the beile Surhaci and others and three thousand men to go; they received five hundred households of the surrounding town, detached three hundred men for Hu Erhan, and sent him ahead as escort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the dingwei year Cemutehei, chief of Feiyoucheng in the Warka, asked to bring his people under the Taizu. Fei Yingdong marched with Surhaci and other beiles and three thousand men, gathered five hundred households from the ring of settlements, detached three hundred soldiers for Hu Erhan, and sent him forward as escort.

sentences.zh: 烏喇貝勒布佔泰發兵萬人要諸途，費英東從諸貝勒督後軍至，大敗烏喇兵。

translations.literal: The Ula beile Buzhantai sent ten thousand men to block the roads. Fei Yingdong came up with the beiles commanding the rear and routed the Ula army.
translations.idiomatic: The Ula beile Buzhantai threw ten thousand men across the route. Fei Yingdong came up with the beiles at the rear and shattered the Ula force.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，太祖命費英東從貝勒巴雅喇伐渥集部，略赫席黑等路，俘二千人以還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer the Taizu ordered Fei Yingdong with the beile Bayara against the Woji tribe, overrunning the Hexihei and other routes and bringing back two thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer the Taizu sent him with Bayara against the Woji, sweeping the Hexihei and neighboring routes and returning with two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥秋七月，渥集部烏爾古宸、木倫二路掠他路太祖所賜甲，太祖命費英東從台吉阿巴泰將千人討之，俘千餘人以還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the year xinhai, the Wuernchen and Mulun routes of the Woji plundered armor the Taizu had bestowed on another route. The Taizu ordered Fei Yingdong with Taiji Abatai and a thousand men to punish them; they returned with more than a thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the xinhai year the Wuernchen and Mulun routes of the Woji raided armor the Taizu had granted another branch. Fei Yingdong marched with Taiji Abatai at the head of a thousand men, punished them, and brought back more than a thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，從太祖伐烏喇，滅之。

translations.literal: In the year guichou he followed the Taizu against Ula and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year he followed the Taizu against Ula and helped destroy it.

sentences.zh: 歲乙卯，太祖將建號，設八旗，命費英東隸鑲黃旗，為左翼固山額真；

translations.literal: In the year yimao, as the Taizu was about to establish his title and set up the Eight Banners, Fei Yingdong was placed in the Bordered Yellow Banner as gushan ejen of the Left Wing;
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year, as the Taizu prepared to proclaim his state and organize the Eight Banners, Fei Yingdong was assigned to the Bordered Yellow Banner as gushan ejen of the Left Wing;

sentences.zh: 置五大臣輔政，以命費英東，仍領一等大臣、扎爾固齊如故。

translations.literal: The Five Great Ministers were appointed to assist in government; Fei Yingdong was named among them, still holding first-rank great minister and Zargaci as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Great Ministers were established to aid rule, and Fei Yingdong was one of them, retaining his first-rank great ministership and the Zargaci post unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年歲丙辰，太祖遂建國，改元天命。

translations.literal: The next year, bingchen, the Taizu founded the state and changed the era name to Tianming.
translations.idiomatic: In the following year, bingchen, the Taizu proclaimed his state and adopted the reign title Tianming.

sentences.zh: 三年，始用兵於明，費英東從攻撫順。

translations.literal: In the third year he first used force against Ming; Fei Yingdong followed the attack on Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he opened hostilities against the Ming; Fei Yingdong joined the assault on Fushun.

sentences.zh: 明總兵張承廕以萬騎來援，據險而陣，火器競發。

translations.literal: The Ming commander Zhang Chengyin came to relieve with ten thousand horsemen, took a strong position, and discharged firearms in volleys.
translations.idiomatic: Ming commander Zhang Chengyin rode to the rescue with ten thousand cavalry, formed on difficult ground, and poured musket fire into the lines.

sentences.zh: 費英東馬驚旁逸，諸軍為之卻，費英東旋馬大呼，麾諸軍並進，遂破之。

translations.literal: Fei Yingdong's horse shied aside and the army fell back for it; he wheeled his horse, shouted loudly, and ordered all troops forward together, and at last broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei Yingdong's mount bolted sideways the whole line wavered; he turned back, roared, and drove every unit forward at once until the Ming force collapsed.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎曰：「此真萬人敵也！」

translations.literal: The Taizu sighed and said, "This is truly a match for ten thousand men!"
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu exclaimed, "Here is a man who could face ten thousand!"

sentences.zh: 四年，明大舉來侵，分道深入。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Ming came in force on many routes deep into our territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Ming launched a major invasion, advancing in separate columns deep into our lands.

sentences.zh: 明總兵杜松屯薩爾滸山巔，費英東所部屬左翼，合諸旗奮擊破之，松戰死，明師以是沮敗。

translations.literal: The Ming commander Du Song encamped on the heights of Sarhu; Fei Yingdong's command was on the Left Wing; all banners charged fiercely and broke them; Song died in battle and the Ming army was thereby discouraged and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ming commander Du Song held the Sarhu heights; Fei Yingdong's division formed the Left Wing. The banners charged together and shattered the enemy; Song fell in battle and the Ming campaign collapsed.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，太祖伐葉赫，費英東從，薄其城，城人飛石投火。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn the Taizu campaigned against Yehe; Fei Yingdong followed, pressed the city, and the defenders hurled stones and fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Taizu marched on Yehe. Fei Yingdong went with him; when they closed on the walls the garrison rained stones and fire.

sentences.zh: 太祖命且退，費英東曰：「我兵已薄城，安可退也？」

translations.literal: The Taizu ordered a temporary withdrawal; Fei Yingdong said, "Our troops have already pressed the city—how can we withdraw?"
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu ordered a pullback. Fei Yingdong protested, "We are already at the walls—how can we pull back now?"

sentences.zh: 又命之，費英東曰：「城垂克，必毋退！」

translations.literal: Ordered again, Fei Yingdong said, "The city is about to fall—we must not retreat!"
translations.idiomatic: When the order came again he said, "The city is within our grasp—we must not retreat!"

sentences.zh: 遂拔其城。

translations.literal: They then stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the assault and took the city.

sentences.zh: 太宗諭金台石降，費英東在側，相與詰責，卒獲金台石，葉赫以是破。

translations.literal: The Taizong urged Jintai Shi to surrender; Fei Yingdong stood at his side and together they pressed him with rebukes; at last Jintai Shi was taken and Yehe was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong called on Jintai Shi to yield; Fei Yingdong stood beside him and both pressed the man with stern rebuke until Jintai Shi was captured and Yehe fell.

sentences.zh: 費英東事太祖，轉戰，每遇敵，身先士卒，戰必勝，攻必克，摧鋒陷陣，當者輒披靡；

translations.literal: Serving the Taizu in campaign after campaign, whenever he met the enemy he led from the front; in battle he always won, in assault he always took; he broke enemy lines and all who faced him scattered;
translations.idiomatic: In every campaign under the Taizu he met the enemy at the head of the column; battle brought victory, assault brought capture; he shattered formations and none who stood before him held firm;

sentences.zh: 國事有闕失，輒強諫，毅然不稍撓：佐太祖成帝業，功最高。

translations.literal: when state affairs went wrong he remonstrated forcefully and would not yield in the least: he aided the Taizu in founding the imperial enterprise, and his merit was the highest.
translations.idiomatic: when policy faltered he spoke bluntly and would not bend; in helping the Taizu build the dynasty his merit stood above all others.

sentences.zh: 五年春三月，太祖定武功爵，授費英東三等總兵官。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in the fifth year the Taizu fixed military merit ranks and granted Fei Yingdong third-rank commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year the Taizu established military peerages and made Fei Yingdong a third-rank commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 是月，費英東卒，年五十有七。

translations.literal: That month Fei Yingdong died at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Fei Yingdong died, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 方疾革，日向西，雲起，有聲鏗鍧，雷電雨雹交至，不移時而霽。

translations.literal: As his illness grew grave, the sun was in the west when clouds rose with a sound like thunder; lightning, rain, and hail came together and in a little while cleared.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of his illness the sun hung in the west when clouds gathered with a thunderous roar; lightning, rain, and hail struck together, then passed as quickly as they had come.

sentences.zh: 太祖將臨喪，諸貝勒以日晏諫，太祖曰：「吾股肱大臣，與同休戚，今先彫喪，吾能無悲乎？」

translations.literal: The Taizu was about to attend the funeral; the beiles urged him because the day was late. The Taizu said, "This minister of mine was arm and thigh; we shared fortune and misfortune. Now he goes before me—how can I not grieve?"
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu meant to go to the bier himself; the beiles pleaded that the hour was late. He said, "This man was my right hand; we shared weal and woe alike. He leaves before me—how could I not mourn?"

sentences.zh: 遂往，哭之慟，至夜分始還。

translations.literal: He went, wept bitterly, and did not return until deep in the night.
translations.idiomatic: He went, wept until he was spent, and did not return until far into the night.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，太祖祭貝勒穆爾哈齊墓，出郊，因至費英東墓，躬奠酒者三，泣數行下。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn the Taizu sacrificed at the tomb of the beile Murhaci, went out of the city, and on the way came to Fei Yingdong's tomb; he personally poured libation three times and wept many lines of tears.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, after sacrificing at the tomb of Beile Murhaci, the Taizu went beyond the walls and stopped at Fei Yingdong's grave; he poured wine himself three times and wept until tears ran in streams.

sentences.zh: 天聰六年，太宗命追封直義公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiancong the Taizong ordered him posthumously enfeoffed as Duke Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tiancong the Taizong posthumously created him Duke Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，始建太廟，以費英東配享。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde the Imperial Ancestral Temple was first built and Fei Yingdong was granted a place in its sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Ancestral Temple was first raised in the first year of Chongde, Fei Yingdong was given a share in its rites.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗諭羣臣曰：「費英東見人不善，必先自斥責而後劾之；

translations.literal: The Taizong once instructed the ministers: "When Fei Yingdong saw a man's fault he first reproached himself and then impeached the man;
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong once told his officials, "When Fei Yingdong saw another's fault he rebuked himself first and only then brought accusation;

sentences.zh: 見人之善，必先自獎勸而後舉之：被劾者無怨言，被舉者亦無驕色。

translations.literal: when he saw a man's merit he first encouraged himself and then recommended the man: those impeached bore no resentment, those recommended showed no pride.
translations.idiomatic: when he saw merit he exhorted himself first and only then advanced the man. The accused harbored no grudge; the promoted showed no arrogance.

sentences.zh: 朕未聞諸臣以善惡直奏如斯人者也！」

translations.literal: I have never heard any minister report good and evil so directly as this man!"
translations.idiomatic: I have never known a minister to lay good and evil so plainly before the throne as he did!"

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，世祖詔曰：「費英東事太祖，參贊廟謨，恢擴疆土，為開創佐命第一功臣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi the Shizu decreed: "Fei Yingdong served the Taizu, assisted in state planning, and widened the frontier— the foremost founding minister. The reward for his line shall not be called by his merit alone; he is advanced to third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi the Shizu proclaimed: "Fei Yingdong served the Taizu, shaped grand strategy, and opened the realm—the first of the founding ministers. Let his house's hereditary reward stand apart from a mere tally of merit; advance his line to third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 延世之賞，勿稱其勳，命進爵為三等公。」

translations.literal: Perpetual bounty—do not name his merit alone; order advancement to third-rank duke."
translations.idiomatic: The perpetual bounty shall not be measured only by his deeds; command that his rank be raised to third-rank duke."

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，聖祖親為文勒碑墓道，稱其功冠諸臣，為一代元勳。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi the Shengzu personally composed the text for a stele at the tomb road, calling his merit foremost among ministers and a founding pillar of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kangxi the Shengzu wrote the tomb-stele inscription himself, declaring his service supreme among the ministers and a founding pillar of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 雍正九年，世宗命加封號曰信勇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongzheng the Shizong ordered the added honorific title Xinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongzheng the Shizong added the posthumous style Xinyong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年，高宗復命進爵為一等公。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong the Gaozong again ordered advancement to first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of Qianlong the Gaozong raised the line again to first-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 費英東子十，圖賴自有傳。

translations.literal: Fei Yingdong had ten sons; Tulai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yingdong had ten sons; Tulai has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 索海，費英東第六子，襲總兵官。

translations.literal: Suo Hai, Fei Yingdong's sixth son, inherited the commander-in-chief rank.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Hai, the sixth son of Fei Yingdong, inherited the commander-in-chief title.

sentences.zh: 旋坐事，奪職。

translations.literal: Soon after he was punished for an offense and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon punished for misconduct and deprived of his post.

sentences.zh: 太宗天聰五年，初置六部，授刑部承政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong under the Taizong the Six Ministries were first established; he was made Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taizong's fifth year of Tiancong, when the Six Ministries were first set up, he was appointed head of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 七年，與兵部承政車爾格偵明邊，至錦州，有所俘馘，命管牛錄事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he joined the Minister of War Cheerge in reconnoitering the Ming border, reached Jinzhou, took captives and heads, and was ordered to manage niru affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined War Minister Cheerge on a probe of the Ming frontier, reached Jinzhou with prisoners and trophies, and was put in charge of niru administration.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，更定部院官制，改都察院左參政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde the ministries and courts were reorganized; he became Left Censor of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongde the ministries were reorganized and he became Left Censor of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十月，從太宗伐明，略大凌河，下屯堡十四，复授刑部承政。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he followed the Taizong against Ming, overran Dalinghe, took fourteen fortified hamlets, and was again made Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he followed the Taizong against the Ming, swept Dalinghe, reduced fourteen stockaded posts, and was again named Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四年，索倫部博木博果爾等降而復叛，命索海及工部承政薩木什喀帥師往討之，克雅克薩、兀庫爾二城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Solon chief Bumboguoer and others submitted then rebelled; Suo Hai and Works Minister Samushika were ordered to lead troops to punish them and took the two cities of Yaksa and Wuku'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Bumboguoer of the Solon and others submitted and then rebelled; Suo Hai and Works Minister Samushika led troops against them and captured Yaksa and Wuku'er.

sentences.zh: 進攻鐸陳城，博木博果爾以六千人來援，乘我師後，索海設伏以待，破敵，俘四百，乘勝入其壘，博木博果爾遁去。

translations.literal: Advancing on Duochen city, Bumboguoer came with six thousand men to relieve, struck our rear; Suo Hai set an ambush, broke the enemy, took four hundred prisoners, pressed into their camp, and Bumboguoer fled.
translations.idiomatic: When they advanced on Duochen, Bumboguoer brought six thousand reinforcements against their rear. Suo Hai laid an ambush, routed the enemy, seized four hundred captives, stormed the camp, and Bumboguoer fled.

sentences.zh: 索海率諸將攻掛喇爾屯，攻克之，屯兵五百，斬級二百，俘百三十還。

translations.literal: Suo Hai led the generals against Gualar tun, took it, left five hundred men garrisoned, slew two hundred, and returned with a hundred thirty prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Hai led the generals against Gualar tun, captured it, left five hundred men as garrison, killed two hundred of the enemy, and returned with one hundred thirty captives.

sentences.zh: 逐敵額蘇里屯西、額爾圖屯東，俘六千九百五十六人，牛羊駝馬稱是。

translations.literal: Pursuing the enemy west of Esuli tun and east of Eertu tun, they took six thousand nine hundred fifty-six people and cattle, sheep, camels, and horses in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the foe west of Esuli tun and east of Eertu tun, they brought in 6,956 captives and livestock in like abundance.

sentences.zh: 師還，命貝勒杜度、阿巴泰迎勞，太宗幸實勝寺，賜宴，敘功，授二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the beiles Dudu and Abatai were ordered to welcome them; the Taizong visited Shisheng Temple, gave a feast, reckoned merit, and granted second-rank jalan gusai.
translations.idiomatic: On their return Beiles Dudu and Abatai were sent to welcome them; the Taizong came to Shisheng Temple, feasted them, tallied merit, and granted second-rank jalan gusai.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾索海行軍不立寨，俘有逋者，當奪賞，命貰之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War impeached Suo Hai for not establishing camp on the march and for escaped prisoners; he should have been stripped of reward, but the order remitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The War Ministry charged Suo Hai with failing to encamp on campaign and with lost prisoners; he should have forfeited his reward, but the throne pardoned the penalty.

sentences.zh: 六年春，從睿親王多爾袞等出師圍錦州，坐私遣官兵歸，離城遠屯，徵還，與譚泰、阿山、葉克書等皆罰鍰。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he followed the Prince Regent Dorgon and others to besiege Jinzhou; for privately sending troops home and encamping far from the city he was recalled; with Tantai, Ashan, Yekešu and others he was all fined.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth spring he joined Prince Regent Dorgon to besiege Jinzhou; for sending troops home without leave and pitching camp too far from the walls he was recalled, and he, Tantai, Ashan, Yekešu, and others were all fined.

sentences.zh: 夏，復從多爾袞等出師圍錦州，城兵出行汲小凌河，索海以兵四百邀擊，斬九十餘級，遂從攻松山，擊破明軍。

translations.literal: In summer he again followed Dorgon and others to besiege Jinzhou; garrison troops went out to draw water at the Xiaoling River; Suo Hai with four hundred men intercepted them and slew more than ninety; he then followed the attack on Songshan and broke the Ming army.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he again besieged Jinzhou with Dorgon; when defenders went to the Xiaoling River for water Suo Hai ambushed them with four hundred men and killed more than ninety, then joined the assault on Songshan and routed the Ming force.

sentences.zh: 時有敏惠恭和元妃之喪，索海召降將祖大樂俳優至其帳歌舞，刑部論索海當死，削職。

translations.literal: At the time of the mourning for the Consort Minhui Gonghe, Suo Hai summoned the surrendered general Zu Dole's entertainers to his tent for song and dance; the Ministry of Punishments judged Suo Hai deserving of death and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for Consort Minhui Gonghe, Suo Hai had entertainers of the surrendered general Zu Dole perform in his tent; Punishments ruled death and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 上使諭之曰：「爾既至篤恭殿及大清門前。」

translations.literal: The sovereign sent word: "You have already come to the Dugong Hall and before the Daqing Gate."
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent word: "You have already come as far as the Dugong Hall and the Daqing Gate—"

sentences.zh: 索海遂坐廢，終太宗世不復用。

translations.literal: Suo Hai was thereby disgraced and was never again employed through the Taizong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Hai was ruined by the scandal and was never employed again while the Taizong lived.

sentences.zh: 世祖順治二年，以副都統從征四川，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi under the Shizu he served as vice dutong on the Sichuan campaign and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shizu's second year of Shunzhi he marched to Sichuan as vice dutong and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 子多頗羅，以從入關擊流賊有勞，授牛錄章京，進一等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: His son Duopiluo, for merit in entering the pass and striking the roving bandits, was granted jalan gusai and advanced to first-rank jalan gusai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duopiluo, for service in entering the pass and fighting the roving rebels, received jalan gusai and was later raised to first-rank jalan gusai.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從信郡王多尼徵雲南，戰死磨盤山。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed Prince Xin Duoni against Yunnan and died in battle at Mopanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he followed Prince Xin Duoni to Yunnan and fell at Mopanshan.

sentences.zh: 倭黑，費英東諸孫。

translations.literal: Wohei, a grandson among Fei Yingdong's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wohei was a grandson in Fei Yingdong's line.

sentences.zh: 父察哈尼。

translations.literal: His father was Chahani.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Chahani.

sentences.zh: 方索海嗣父爵而黜也，太宗以納海、圖賴分襲，既又以事奪爵，復以察哈尼襲。

translations.literal: When Suo Hai had inherited his father's rank and was then removed, the Taizong had Nohai and Tulai divide the inheritance; later their ranks were also taken for offenses, and Chahani inherited again.
translations.idiomatic: When Suo Hai inherited and was then dismissed, the Taizong split the title between Nohai and Tulai; when they too lost rank for offenses, Chahani inherited again.

sentences.zh: 尋改三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: Soon after it was changed to third-rank angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: The title was soon changed to third-rank angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 卒，子倭黑，襲。

translations.literal: When he died his son Wohei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Wohei succeeded.

sentences.zh: 世祖初元，從入關。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shizu's reign he followed the entry into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shizu's reign he marched through the pass into China proper.

sentences.zh: 四年，復更定爵秩，改三等精奇尼哈番，遇恩詔累進一等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the peerage was fixed anew; it became third-rank jingqiniha fan, and under grace edicts was repeatedly advanced by one degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year ranks were redefined; he held third-rank jingqiniha fan, and amnesty edicts raised him step by step.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進三等公，並授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was advanced to third-rank duke and also made a grand minister of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was raised to third-rank duke and appointed grand minister of the interior.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，聖祖譴鼇拜，吏部議倭黑與同族，當黜，命罷內大臣，隸驍騎營。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, when the Shengzu punished Oboi, the Board of Civil Appointments judged Wohei of the same clan and fit for dismissal; he was removed as interior minister and placed in the Vanguard Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi's eighth year, when the Shengzu moved against Oboi, the Board judged Wohei kin to the faction and due for removal; he lost his interior post and was assigned to the Vanguard Brigade.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，倭黑從征。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled Wohei joined the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in rebellion Wohei took the field.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命以署副都統率兗州駐防兵，佐定南將軍希爾根進討，敗耿精忠將左宗邦於分宜，敗吳三桂將硃君聘、黃乃忠於袁州，遂收安福。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered as acting vice dutong to lead the Yanzhou garrison and assist the Pacifier of the South Xiergen; he defeated Geng Jingzhong's general Zuo Zongbang at Fenyi and Wu Sangui's generals Zhu Junpin and Huang Naizhong at Yuanzhou, then recovered Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was named acting vice dutong, led the Yanzhou garrison, and aided Pacifier of the South Xiergen; he beat Zuo Zongbang of Geng Jingzhong at Fenyi and Zhu Junpin and Huang Naizhong of Wu Sangui at Yuanzhou, then recovered Anfu.

sentences.zh: 擊賊鸞石嶺、白水口，屢捷。

translations.literal: Striking rebels at Luanshiling and Baishuikou he won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: At Luanshiling and Baishuikou he struck the rebels again and again with success.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he received the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍安親王岳樂复萍鄉，至長沙，擊敗吳三桂兵。

translations.literal: He followed the commander Prince An Yuele in recovering Pingxiang, reached Changsha, and defeated Wu Sangui's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Commander Prince An Yuele in retaking Pingxiang, advanced to Changsha, and routed Wu Sangui's force.

sentences.zh: 十六年，岳樂分兵授倭黑，令駐茶陵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Yuele detached troops for Wohei and ordered him to garrison Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Yuele gave Wohei a separate command and stationed him at Chaling.

sentences.zh: 十七年，移屯攸縣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he moved camp to Youxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he shifted his camp to Youxian.

sentences.zh: 十八年，從大將軍貝子彰泰下雲南，授鑲黃旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he followed the commander Prince Zhangtai south into Yunnan and was made vice dutong of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he followed Commander Prince Zhangtai into Yunnan and was made Mongol vice dutong of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，二十一年，擢都統。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified, in the twenty-first year he was promoted to dutong.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan was pacified, in the twenty-first year he was promoted to dutong.

sentences.zh: 議政大臣議諸將帥功罪，以倭黑擊賊長沙嘗引退，當譴，命罷太子太保。

translations.literal: Grand councilors weighed the merits and faults of the commanders; because Wohei had once fallen back while fighting rebels at Changsha he was due censure and was stripped of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Councilors reviewed the generals' merits and faults; because Wohei had once withdrawn at Changsha he was censured and lost the Grand Guardian title.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirtieth year.

sentences.zh: 子傅爾丹，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Fuerdan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuerdan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 何和禮，棟鄂氏，其先自瓦爾喀遷於棟鄂，別為一部，因以地為姓。

translations.literal: He Heli was of the Donggo clan; his ancestors moved from Warka to Donggo, became a separate tribe, and took the place as surname.
translations.idiomatic: He Heli belonged to the Donggo clan. His forebears had moved from Warka to Donggo, formed a separate tribe, and took the place-name as their clan.

sentences.zh: 何和禮祖曰克徹巴顏，父曰額勒吉，兄曰屯珠魯巴顏，世為其部長。

translations.literal: He Heli's grandfather was called Kezhebayan, his father Eleji, his elder brother Tunzhulubayan; for generations they were chiefs of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Kezhebayan, his father Eleji, his elder brother Tunzhulubayan; for generations they had headed the tribe.

sentences.zh: 何和禮年二十六，代兄長其部。

translations.literal: At twenty-six He Heli replaced his brother as head of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-six He Heli succeeded his brother as tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 棟鄂部素強，克徹巴顏與章甲城長阿哈納相仇怨。

translations.literal: The Donggo tribe had long been strong; Kezhebayan and Zhangjiacheng chief Ahana were at feud.
translations.idiomatic: The Donggo had long been powerful; Kezhebayan and Ahana, chief of Zhangjiacheng, nursed a bitter feud.

sentences.zh: 阿哈納，興祖諸孫，為「寧古塔」六貝勒之一。

translations.literal: Ahana, a descendant of Xingzu, was one of the six beiles of "Ningguta."
translations.idiomatic: Ahana, a descendant of Xingzu, was one of the six beiles of Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 棟鄂屢侵寧古塔，寧古塔借兵哈達伐棟鄂，互攻掠。

translations.literal: Donggo repeatedly raided Ningguta; Ningguta borrowed troops from Hada to campaign against Donggo, and they raided each other.
translations.idiomatic: Donggo raided Ningguta again and again; Ningguta borrowed Hada troops to strike back, and the two sides harried one another.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起兵，聞何和禮所部兵馬精壯，乃加禮招致之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu first raised his army he heard that He Heli's troops and horses were excellent and sent special courtesies to win him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu first took up arms he heard that He Heli's warriors and horses were first-rate and sent him marked honors to win him over.

sentences.zh: 歲戊子，太祖納哈達女為妃，行。

translations.literal: In the year wuzi the Taizu took a daughter of Hada as consort and set out on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuzi year the Taizu married a daughter of Hada and set out on the wedding journey.

sentences.zh: 比還，遂以所部來附，太祖以長女妻焉。

translations.literal: On his return He Heli at once came with his tribe to submit; the Taizu gave him the eldest princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back He Heli brought his whole tribe to submit, and the Taizu gave him his eldest princess as wife.

sentences.zh: 何和禮故有妻，挾所部留故？

translations.literal: He Heli had a former wife who took part of the tribe and remained in the old territory.
translations.idiomatic: He Heli already had a wife who held part of the tribe back in the old lands.

sentences.zh: 何和禮率三十騎地者，求與何和禮戰，太祖面諭之，乃罷兵降。

translations.literal: Those who stayed in the old territory demanded battle with He Heli; the Taizu admonished them in person and they ceased fighting and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The people left behind demanded a fight with He Heli; the Taizu rebuked them face to face until they laid down arms and submitted.

sentences.zh: 旗制初定，何和禮所部隸紅旗，為本旗總管。

translations.literal: When the banner system was first fixed He Heli's following was placed in the Plain Red Banner as head of that banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the banners were first organized his people entered the Plain Red Banner and he became its chief.

sentences.zh: 歲戊申，從太祖徵烏喇，率本旗兵破敵有功。

translations.literal: In the year wushen he followed the Taizu against Ula, led his banner troops to break the enemy with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the wushen year he joined the Taizu against Ula and led his banner to defeat the enemy with credit.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥，太祖命與額亦都、扈爾漢將兵伐渥集部虎爾哈路，克扎庫塔城。

translations.literal: In the year xinhai the Taizu ordered him with E Yidu and Hu Erhan to lead troops against the Hu'erha route of the Woji tribe and took Zhakuta city.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinhai year the Taizu sent him with E Yidu and Hu Erhan against the Hu'erha route of the Woji; they captured Zhakuta.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，從太祖再徵烏喇。

translations.literal: In the year guichou he followed the Taizu in a second campaign against Ula.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year he joined the Taizu's second expedition against Ula.

sentences.zh: 太祖招諭布佔泰，猶冀其悛悔，何和禮與諸貝勒力請進攻，遂滅烏喇。

translations.literal: The Taizu summoned Buzhantai to yield, still hoping he would repent; He Heli and the beiles urgently asked to attack, and Ula was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu still hoped Buzhantai might repent and urged him to submit; He Heli and the beiles pressed for an assault, and Ula was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 天命建元，旗制更定，何和禮所部隸正紅旗。

translations.literal: When Tianming was inaugurated and the banners were reorganized, He Heli's following was placed in the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Tianming, when the banners were redrawn, his people were assigned to the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 置五大臣，何和禮與焉。

translations.literal: The Five Great Ministers were appointed; He Heli was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Great Ministers were named, He Heli stood among them.

sentences.zh: 四年，從破明經略楊鎬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the defeat of Ming Grand Coordinator Yang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined the victory over Ming Grand Coordinator Yang Hao.

sentences.zh: 六年，下瀋陽、遼陽，何和禮皆在行間，敘功，授三等總兵官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shenyang and Liaoyang fell; He Heli was always in the ranks; for merit he was granted third-rank commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Shenyang and Liaoyang were taken; He Heli marched throughout and was made third-rank commander-in-chief for his service.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，卒，年六十有四。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year he died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year he died, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 時費英東、額亦都、安費揚古、扈爾漢皆前卒，太祖哭之慟，曰：「朕所與並肩友好諸大臣，何不遺一人以送朕老耶？」

translations.literal: By then Fei Yingdong, E Yidu, Anfiyanggu, and Hu Erhan had all died before him. The Taizu mourned bitterly and said, "Of the great ministers who stood shoulder to shoulder with me in friendship, why did not one remain to see me into old age?"
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yingdong, E Yidu, Anfiyanggu, and Hu Erhan had all gone before him. The Taizu wept bitterly and said, "Of the ministers who stood shoulder to shoulder with me, could not one have stayed to see me into old age?"

sentences.zh: 太宗朝，進爵為三等公。

translations.literal: Under the Taizong his rank was advanced to third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taizong his line was raised to third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，追諡溫順，勒石紀功。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously styled Wenshun and a stele was carved to record his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he received the posthumous name Wenshun and a stone was carved to his honor.

sentences.zh: 雍正九年，加封號曰勇勤。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongzheng the added honorific Yongqin was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongzheng the supplemental style Yongqin was added.

sentences.zh: 子六。

translations.literal: He had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left six sons.

sentences.zh: 多積禮，何和禮次子。

translations.literal: Duo Jili, He Heli's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Jili was He Heli's second son.

sentences.zh: 初授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: He was first granted niru daikan.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made niru daikan.

sentences.zh: 事四貝勒，從伐烏拉。

translations.literal: He served the Fourth Beile and followed the campaign against Ula.
translations.idiomatic: He attended the Fourth Beile and joined the war against Ula.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，擢甲喇額真。

translations.literal: Under Tiancong he was promoted to jalan daikan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancong era he rose to jalan daikan.

sentences.zh: 從伐錦州，圍大凌河，授游擊世職。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against Jinzhou, besieged Dalinghe, and was granted the hereditary rank of guerrilla officer.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Jinzhou, helped besiege Dalinghe, and received a hereditary guerrilla command.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，帥師伐東海瓦爾喀部，俘壯丁三百餘，擢本旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he led troops against the Eastern Sea Warka tribe, took more than three hundred able-bodied men, and was promoted to meiren daikan of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde's first year he commanded against the Eastern Sea Warka, brought back more than three hundred fighting men, and was made meiren daikan of his banner.

sentences.zh: 四年，與鎮國公扎喀納率兵屯籓、屏二城間，卒竊馬遁去，追之勿及。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, with Prince Guoguo Zhakana he stationed troops between Fan and Ping; a soldier stole horses and fled; pursuit did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he camped between Fan and Ping with Prince Guoguo Zhakana; a trooper stole horses and escaped beyond pursuit.

sentences.zh: 論罪，奪世職，籍沒，上命留弓矢、甲胄及三馬，仍領梅勒額真事。

translations.literal: Judged guilty, he lost his hereditary office and his property was confiscated; the sovereign ordered that bow, arrows, armor, and three horses be left him, and he still led meiren daikan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted, he forfeited his hereditary post and his goods were seized; the throne let him keep bow, arrows, armor, and three horses, and he continued as meiren daikan.

sentences.zh: 六年，從擊洪承疇，率騎兵循。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the attack on Hong Chengchou and led cavalry in pursuit along the coast.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the campaign against Hong Chengchou and led cavalry in coastal pursuit.

sentences.zh: 七年，以老罷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was retired for age.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he stepped down on account of age.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 和碩圖，何和禮四子。

translations.literal: Heshuotu, He Heli's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Heshuotu was He Heli's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初襲三等總兵官。

translations.literal: He first inherited third-rank commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He first succeeded to third-rank commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 太祖以大貝勒代善女妻焉，號和碩額駙。

translations.literal: The Taizu gave him the senior beile Daishan's daughter in marriage and styled him Heshuo Efu.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu married him to Daishan's daughter and styled him Heshuo Efu, imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，授正紅旗固山額真。

translations.literal: When the Taizong took the throne he was made gushan ejen of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At the Taizong's accession he became gushan ejen of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從擊朝鮮，又從伐明，攻錦州、寧遠有功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed the strike on Korea and again campaigned against Ming, attacking Jinzhou and Ningyuan with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong's first year he joined the Korean expedition and the Ming campaigns, distinguishing himself at Jinzhou and Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 二年，從貝勒阿巴泰帥師破錦州、杏山、松山諸路。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Beile Abatai in breaking the routes of Jinzhou, Xingshan, and Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he marched with Beile Abatai and broke the Jinzhou, Xingshan, and Songshan lines.

sentences.zh: 九月，复伐察哈爾，克其四路軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again campaigned against Chahar and defeated its four-route army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he campaigned again against Chahar and overthrew its four-route force.

sentences.zh: 以功加五牛錄，進爵三等公。

translations.literal: For merit five niru were added to his command and his rank was advanced to third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: For his service five niru were added and he was raised to third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 三年，從貝勒岳託帥師攻大安口，敗明戍兵於馬蘭峪，再敗明援兵於石門寨。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Beile Yuetuo in attacking Da'ankou, defeated Ming garrison troops at Malanyu, and again defeated Ming relief at Shimenzhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Beile Yuetuo against Da'ankou, routed Ming defenders at Malanyu, and beat Ming reinforcements at Shimenzhai.

sentences.zh: 復從太宗攻遵化，率本旗兵攻其城西北，克之。

translations.literal: He again followed the Taizong against Zunhua, led his banner troops against the northwest of the city, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Taizong again at Zunhua, led his banner against the northwest wall, and carried the place.

sentences.zh: 師薄燕京，結營土城關，明兵來攻，擊卻之。

translations.literal: The army pressed Yanjing and encamped at Tuchengguan; Ming troops came to attack and were driven back.
translations.idiomatic: The army closed on Yanjing and pitched camp at Tuchengguan; when Ming forces attacked they were thrown back.

sentences.zh: 复敗明師於盧溝橋，與副都統阿山等陣斬明武經略滿桂、總兵孫祖壽，獲黑雲龍、麻登雲。

translations.literal: He again defeated Ming troops at Lugou Bridge; with vice dutong Ashan and others he slew in battle Ming Military Affairs Commissioner Man Gui and commander Sun Zushou, and captured Heiyunlong and Madengyun.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Ming troops again at Lugou Bridge; with Ashan and other officers he killed Man Gui, Ming commissioner of military affairs, and Sun Zushou in the line, and took Heiyunlong and Madengyun prisoner.

sentences.zh: 師旋，克永平，帥騎兵守灤州。

translations.literal: When the army turned back it took Yongping; he led cavalry to hold Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Yongping fell; he commanded cavalry to garrison Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，從圍大凌河城，以本旗兵當其西北。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he joined the siege of Dalinghe and posted his banner on the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he helped besiege Dalinghe with his banner on the northwest sector.

sentences.zh: 明兵突圍出，與都統葉臣等夾擊破之，追奔及城壕而還。

translations.literal: Ming troops broke out; with dutong Yechen and others he struck them from both sides, broke them, pursued to the moat, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming troops sallied out he and Dutong Yechen caught them in a pincer, shattered them, chased them to the moat, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七年，上詢伐明及朝鮮、察哈爾三國何先，和碩圖疏言：「宜先葺治諸城堡，乃覘明邊，乘瑕而入。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the sovereign asked whether Ming, Korea, or Chahar should be attacked first. Heshuotu memorialized: "The various forts should first be repaired; then probe the Ming border and enter where there is an opening.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the court asked which enemy to strike first—Ming, Korea, or Chahar. Heshuotu advised: "Repair the frontier forts first, then watch the Ming border and strike wherever it is weak.

sentences.zh: 若天佑我，各城納款，勢不能速歸，南界六城，立界屯耕，修築可差後。

translations.literal: If Heaven favors us and the cities submit, we cannot return quickly; for the six southern border towns establish boundary garrisons and farming—their repair can wait.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven favors us and towns yield, we cannot march home at once; garrison and farm the six southern border posts—those works can come later.

sentences.zh: 慮我兵既出，敵伺其隙，鞭長不及，難為援也。

translations.literal: I fear that once our troops are out the enemy will watch for openings; the whip cannot reach far enough to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: But once our armies are abroad the enemy will watch for gaps; aid cannot reach them in time.

sentences.zh: 瀋陽、牛莊、耀州三城宜先繕完，庶邊界內外皆可長驅。」

translations.literal: Shenyang, Niuzhuang, and Yaozhou should be finished first so that inside and outside the frontier we may drive deep in every direction."
translations.idiomatic: Finish Shenyang, Niuzhuang, and Yaozhou first, so the whole frontier, within and without, lies open to a long advance."

sentences.zh: 七月，和碩圖卒，上親臨哭之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Heshuotu died and the sovereign came in person to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month and the sovereign mourned at his bier in person.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，追諡端恪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously styled Duankuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he received the posthumous name Duankuo.

sentences.zh: 都類，何和禮第五子，公主出也。

translations.literal: Dulei, He Heli's fifth son, born of the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Dulei was He Heli's fifth son, child of the imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 初為牛錄額真，洊擢本旗固山額真。

translations.literal: He was first niru daikan and was repeatedly promoted to gushan ejen of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: He began as niru daikan and rose step by step to gushan ejen of his banner.

sentences.zh: 以公主子，增領兩牛錄。

translations.literal: As son of the princess he received charge of two additional niru.
translations.idiomatic: As the princess's son he was given two extra niru.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從太宗伐朝鮮，薄漢城，先登，城潰，率阿禮哈超哈兵入城搜剿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed the Taizong against Korea, pressed Hancheng, was first to climb the wall; when the city broke he led Alha Chaoha troops into the city to search and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde's first year he joined the Korean campaign, closed on Hancheng, and was first over the wall; when it fell he led Alha Chaoha men through the streets to hunt down resistance.

sentences.zh: 以失察所部違法亂行，罰鍰，奪所分俘獲。

translations.literal: For failure to restrain his men from illegal disorder he was fined and stripped of his share of captives.
translations.idiomatic: Because his troops had run wild without restraint he was fined and lost his share of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 三年，從貝勒岳託伐明，次密雲牆子嶺。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Beile Yuetuo against Ming and halted at Miyun Qiangziling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Beile Yuetuo against the Ming and camped at Miyun Qiangziling.

sentences.zh: 明將以三千人來拒，都類與譚泰督部將夾擊，大敗之，獲馬百、駝二十。

translations.literal: A Ming commander came with three thousand men to resist; Dulei with Tantai directed the subordinate generals in a pincer attack, routed them, and took a hundred horses and twenty camels.
translations.idiomatic: A Ming officer advanced with three thousand men; Dulei and Tantai directed a double envelopment, crushed them, and seized a hundred horses and twenty camels.

sentences.zh: 軍分四道進，所當輒摧破，略地至濟南而還。

translations.literal: The army advanced in four columns; wherever they met the enemy they broke them and overran the country as far as Jinan before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The army moved in four columns, shattered every force in its path, and raided as far as Jinan before turning home.

sentences.zh: 四年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗圍錦州，坐所部退縮，又受蒙古饋遺，罰鍰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang in besieging Jinzhou; because his troops fell back he was fined, and he also accepted Mongol gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined Prince Zheng Jirhalang at Jinzhou; his men had given ground and he had taken Mongol gifts, so he was fined.

sentences.zh: 未幾，所部訐告都類在山東時，縱廝養盜馬，私發明德王埋藏珍物，坐論死，上貸之，奪職，籍沒。

translations.literal: Before long his troops reported that while in Shandong Dulei had let servants steal horses and privately opened treasures buried by Prince Mingde; he was judged deserving of death; the sovereign pardoned him but removed office and confiscated property.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his men accused him of letting servants steal horses in Shandong and opening Prince Mingde's buried treasure; death was the sentence, but the throne spared his life, stripped his post, and seized his goods.

sentences.zh: 八年，復起為固山額真，鎮錦州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was restored as gushan ejen and garrisoned Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was brought back as gushan ejen to hold Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，從肅親王豪格徵張獻忠，分兵定慶陽，會師西充，擊殺獻忠，與貝勒尼堪等戡定川北州縣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong, detached troops to secure Qingyang, joined at Xichong, killed Xianzhong, and with Beile Nikan and others pacified the prefectures of northern Sichuan.
