translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi's third year he marched with Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong, detached a force to take Qingyang, united at Xichong, killed Xianzhong, and with Beile Nikan pacified northern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 師還，論功，並遇恩詔，累進二等伯。

translations.literal: When the army returned merit was reckoned; with grace edicts he was repeatedly advanced to second-rank count.
translations.idiomatic: On return his merit was tallied; grace edicts raised him repeatedly to second-rank count.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 安費揚古，覺爾察氏，世居瑚濟寨。

translations.literal: Anfiyanggu was of the Juercha clan and for generations his family dwelt at Huji stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Anfiyanggu belonged to the Juercha clan; his people had long lived at the Huji stockade.

sentences.zh: 父完布祿，事太祖，有章甲、尼麻喇人誘之叛，不從，又劫其孫以要之，終無貳志。

translations.literal: His father Wanbulu served the Taizu. Men of Zhangjia and Nimara tempted him to rebel; he would not. They also seized his grandson to coerce him, yet he never wavered.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wanbulu served the Taizu. Zhangjia and Nimara men tempted him to rebel, but he refused; they even seized his grandson to force him, yet he never wavered.

sentences.zh: 安費揚古少事太祖。

translations.literal: Anfiyanggu attended the Taizu from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Anfiyanggu had served the Taizu since boyhood.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed he was placed in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the banners were organized he entered the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 歲癸未，太祖兵初起，仇尼堪外蘭，克圖倫城，攻甲版。

translations.literal: In the year guiwei, when the Taizu's army was first raised, he avenged Nikhan Wailan, took Tulun city, and attacked Jiaban.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year, when the Taizu first took up arms, he campaigned against Nikhan Wailan, stormed Tulun, and attacked Jiaban.

sentences.zh: 薩爾滸城長諾米訥、柰喀達陰助尼堪外蘭，漏師期，尼堪外蘭得遁去。

translations.literal: Nuomine and Naikada, chiefs of Sarhü city, secretly aided Nikhan Wailan and leaked the date of our march, so Nikhan Wailan escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Nuomine and Naikada of Sarhü secretly helped Nikhan Wailan and revealed the date of our march, letting him escape.

sentences.zh: 太祖憾諾米訥、柰喀達，執而殺之，使安費揚古率兵取其城。

translations.literal: The Taizu resented Nuomine and Naikada, seized and killed them, and sent Anfiyanggu with troops to take their city.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu hated Nuomine and Naikada, executed them, and sent Anfiyanggu to take their city.

sentences.zh: 康嘉者，太祖再從兄弟也，惎太祖英武，與羣從謀以哈達兵至，俾兆佳城長李岱為導，劫瑚濟寨。

translations.literal: Kangjia, a second cousin of the Taizu, envied the Taizu's valor and with kinsmen plotted to bring Hada troops; Li Dai, chief of Zhaojia city, would guide them to raid the Huji stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Kangjia, the Taizu's second cousin, envied his prowess and plotted with kinsmen to bring Hada troops; Li Dai of Zhaojia would guide a raid on Huji.

sentences.zh: 既，引去，安費揚古方獵，聞有兵，與巴遜以十二人追及，擊破之。

translations.literal: After they withdrew Anfiyanggu was hunting; hearing of troops he and Bassun with twelve men pursued, overtook them, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When they withdrew Anfiyanggu was hunting; hearing soldiers abroad he and Bassun with twelve men overtook and routed them.

sentences.zh: 歲甲申正月，從太祖攻兆佳城，獲李岱。

translations.literal: In the first month of the year jiashen he followed the Taizu in attacking Zhaojia city and captured Li Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the jiashen year he joined the Taizu against Zhaojia and took Li Dai.

sentences.zh: 其黨李古里扎泰走附汪泰，安費揚古以太祖命往諭，並汪泰降之。

translations.literal: Their partisan Liguli Zhatai fled to join Wangtai; Anfiyanggu went by the Taizu's order to summon him, and Wangtai also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The partisan Liguli Zhatai fled to Wangtai; Anfiyanggu went under orders to summon him, and Wangtai submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 六月，從太祖攻馬兒墩寨，寨負險，守者甚備，矢石雜下，攻三日不克。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he followed the Taizu against the Maerdun stockade; the stockade stood on difficult ground and the defenders were well prepared; arrows and stones rained down; for three days the assault failed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he joined the assault on Maerdun; the place was steep, the defense stout, and arrows and stones poured down for three days without success.

sentences.zh: 安費揚古夜率兵自間道攀崖而上，拔其寨。

translations.literal: Anfiyanggu led troops by night on a hidden path up the cliff and stormed the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Anfiyanggu climbed by night along a hidden path and stormed the stockade.

sentences.zh: 歲丁亥六月，太祖伐哲陳部，八月，克洞城，歲戊子九月，克王甲城，安費揚古皆從戰有功。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the year dinghai the Taizu campaigned against the Zhecen tribe; in the eighth month he took Dong city; in the ninth month of the year wuzi he took Wangjia city—Anfiyanggu followed every battle with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of dinghai the Taizu struck the Zhecen; in the eighth month Dong fell; in the ninth month of wuzi Wangjia fell—Anfiyanggu fought in each with credit.

sentences.zh: 尋攻克章甲、尼麻喇、赫徹穆諸城，又取香潭寨；

translations.literal: He then took Zhangjia, Nimara, Hechemu, and other cities, and also captured Xiangtan stockade;
translations.idiomatic: He next reduced Zhangjia, Nimara, Hechemu, and other towns, and seized Xiangtan stockade;

sentences.zh: 其長李墩拜湖遁走，追及於碩郭之陽，俘以獻。

translations.literal: its chief Li Dunbaihu fled; they overtook him on the sunny slope of Shuoguo and presented him captive.
translations.idiomatic: its chief Li Dunbaihu fled but was caught on the sunny side of Shuoguo and brought in captive.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳六月，太祖略哈達富爾佳齊寨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the year guisi the Taizu overran the Hada Fuerjiaqi stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the guisi year the Taizu overran the Hada Fuerjiaqi stockade.

sentences.zh: 師還，太祖躬勒兵以殿，哈達貝勒孟格布祿率騎追至，一騎出太祖前，太祖方引弓射，復有三騎突至，太祖馬幾墜，三騎揮刀來犯，安費揚古截擊，盡斬之；

translations.literal: When the army returned the Taizu personally commanded the rearguard; the Hada beile Menggebulu pursued with cavalry. One horseman rode out before the Taizu as he was drawing his bow; then three more burst forward; the Taizu's horse nearly fell; the three horsemen slashed at him; Anfiyanggu intercepted and cut them all down;
translations.idiomatic: On the return the Taizu led the rearguard himself. Menggebulu of Hada pursued with cavalry. One rider darted ahead while the Taizu strung his bow; three more charged in and nearly unhorsed him; Anfiyanggu cut them all down;

sentences.zh: 太祖亦射孟格布祿中馬踣，敵騎敗走。

translations.literal: the Taizu also shot Menggebulu's horse so that it fell, and the enemy cavalry fled.
translations.idiomatic: the Taizu also shot Menggebulu's mount from under him and the enemy horsemen fled.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其勇，賜號碩翁科羅巴圖魯。

translations.literal: The Taizu praised his courage and granted the title Suowenkolo Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu praised his valor and gave him the title Suowenkolo Baturu.

sentences.zh: 九月，太祖既破九部師，閏十一月，命與額亦都、噶蓋等攻訥殷路佛多和山寨，斬其長搜穩塞克什。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, after the Taizu had broken the nine tribes' army, in the intercalary eleventh month he was ordered with E Yidu, Gagai, and others to attack the Neyinlu Foduohe mountain stockade and behead the chief Suwensakexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, after the nine-tribe coalition was broken, in the intercalary eleventh month he joined E Yidu and Gagai against the Neyinlu stockade on Mount Foduohe and beheaded Suwensakexi.

sentences.zh: 歲己亥九月，從太祖滅哈達。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the year jihai he followed the Taizu in destroying Hada.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the jihai year he followed the Taizu in destroying Hada.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥七月，命與台吉阿巴泰等伐渥集部烏爾古宸、木倫二路，取其地，俘其人以歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the year xinhai he was ordered with Taiji Abatai and others against the Wuernchen and Mulun routes of the Woji tribe; they took the territory and returned with captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the xinhai year he marched with Taiji Abatai against the Wuernchen and Mulun routes of the Woji, took their lands, and returned with prisoners.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑正月，從太祖滅烏喇，師薄城，安費揚古執纛先登。

translations.literal: In the first month of the year guichou he followed the Taizu in destroying Ula; when the army pressed the city Anfiyanggu seized the banner and was first to climb.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the guichou year he helped destroy Ula; when the army closed on the walls he took the standard and was first over.

sentences.zh: 尋置五大臣，安費揚古與焉。

translations.literal: Soon the Five Great Ministers were appointed; Anfiyanggu was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Great Ministers were named, Anfiyanggu stood among them.

sentences.zh: 天命元年七月，命與扈爾漢帥師伐東海薩哈連部，至兀爾簡河，刳木為舟，水陸並進，取河南北三十六寨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Tianming he was ordered with Hu Erhan to lead troops against the Eastern Sea Sahalian tribe; at the Wuerjian River they hollowed logs for boats and advanced by land and water, taking thirty-six stockades north and south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianming's first year he and Hu Erhan led troops against the Eastern Sea Sahalian; at the Wuerjian they hollowed logs into boats, advanced by land and water, and took thirty-six stockades on both banks.

sentences.zh: 八月丁巳，師至黑龍江之陽，江水常以九月始冰，是日當駐師處獨冰，寬將六十步，若浮梁。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi of the eighth month the army reached the south bank of the Amur. The river usually begins to freeze in the ninth month; at the place where they were to halt only that day it froze, about sixty paces wide, like a floating bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi of the eighth month they reached the south bank of the Amur. The river normally freezes in the ninth month; that day alone ice formed sixty paces wide where they camped, like a bridge of planks.

sentences.zh: 安費揚古曰：「此天佑我國也！」

translations.literal: Anfiyanggu said, "This is Heaven aiding our state!"
translations.idiomatic: Anfiyanggu cried, "Heaven is aiding our state!"

sentences.zh: 策騎先涉，眾競從之，遂取江北十一寨，降使犬、諾洛、石拉忻三路。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse to cross first; all vied to follow; they then took eleven stockades north of the river and received the submission of the Quan, Nuoluo, and Shilaxin routes.
translations.idiomatic: He rode first across; the whole army followed; they took eleven northern stockades and received the Quan, Nuoluo, and Shilaxin routes.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，太祖取撫順，明總兵張承廕等赴援，分為三營，安費揚古擊其左營，大破之，遂乘勝取三岔兒諸堡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year the Taizu took Fushun; Ming commander Zhang Chengyin and others came to relieve; they divided into three camps; Anfiyanggu struck the left camp, broke it utterly, and pressed on to take the forts of Sancha'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year Fushun fell; Zhang Chengyin and other Ming commanders came in three camps; Anfiyanggu shattered the left camp and swept on to the Sancha'er forts.

sentences.zh: 四年，破明經略楊鎬，滅葉赫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he broke Ming Grand Coordinator Yang Hao and destroyed Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he helped defeat Yang Hao and destroy Yehe.

sentences.zh: 六年，取瀋陽、遼陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shenyang and Liaoyang were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Shenyang and Liaoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 安費揚古皆在行間。

translations.literal: Anfiyanggu was always in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Anfiyanggu marched in every campaign.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year he died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of the seventh year, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，追諡敏壯，立碑紀其功。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously styled Minzhuang and a stele was erected to record his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he received the posthumous name Minzhuang and a monument was raised to his deeds.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗諭羣臣曰：「昔達海、庫爾？

translations.literal: The Taizong once instructed the ministers: "In former days Dahai and Kurha
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong once told his officials, "Long ago Dahai and Kurha

sentences.zh: 勸朕用漢衣冠，朕謂非用武所宜。

translations.literal: urged me to adopt Han dress; I said it was not fitting for the use of arms.
translations.idiomatic: urged me to adopt Han dress, but I said that was no fit way to wage war.

sentences.zh: 我等寬袍大袖，有如安費揚古、勞薩其人者，挺身突入，能御之乎？」

translations.literal: We wear wide robes and large sleeves; if men like Anfiyanggu and Laosa charge in bodily, can they be withstood?"
translations.idiomatic: We wear wide coats and long sleeves; when men like Anfiyanggu and Laosa plunge in bodily, who can stand against them?"

sentences.zh: 當日猛士如雲，而二人尤傑出雲。

translations.literal: In those days fierce warriors were as thick as clouds, yet these two stood tallest among them.
translations.idiomatic: In those days warriors crowded the field like clouds, yet these two towered above the rest.

sentences.zh: 子達爾岱、阿爾岱、碩爾輝。

translations.literal: His sons were Daerdai, Aerdai, and Shuoerhui.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Daerdai, Aerdai, and Shuoerhui.

sentences.zh: 達爾岱以甲喇額眞事太宗。

translations.literal: Daerdai served the Taizong as jalan daikan.
translations.idiomatic: Daerdai served the Taizong as jalan daikan.

sentences.zh: 伐明，攻大凌河，守臧家堡，取錦州、寧遠，徵朝鮮，皆有功。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Ming he attacked Dalinghe, held Zangjiabao, took Jinzhou and Ningyuan, and campaigned against Korea—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Ming he fought at Dalinghe, held Zangjiabao, took Jinzhou and Ningyuan, and campaigned in Korea with credit each time.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，授拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was granted tosahala ha fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi he received tosahala ha fan.

sentences.zh: 七年，追敘<ref>“敘”，原典作“敍”。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, in recording Anfiyanggu's merit, the original text writes xu with the variant form noted in the source.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Anfiyanggu's merit was tallied, the source uses an alternate character for "record" that the editors note.

sentences.zh: </ref>安費揚古功，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He was advanced to first-rank adahaba fan.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to first-rank adahaba fan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年，聖祖念安費揚古開國勳，別授三等阿達哈哈番，令其孫明岱分襲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi the Shengzu, remembering Anfiyanggu's founding merit, separately granted third-rank adahaba fan and had his grandson Mingdai divide the inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi's fifty-second year the Shengzu, mindful of Anfiyanggu's founding service, granted a separate third-rank adahaba fan for his grandson Mingdai to share the succession.

sentences.zh: 阿爾岱子都爾德及碩爾輝孫遜塔，皆有功，受爵世祖朝，別有傳。

translations.literal: Aerdai's son Duerde and Shuoerhui's grandson Sunta all had merit and received ranks under the Shizu; each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Aerdai's son Duerde and Shuoerhui's grandson Sunta also won distinction and ranks under the Shizu; each has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 扈爾漢，佟佳氏，世居雅爾古寨。

translations.literal: Hu Erhan was of the Tong clan and for generations his family dwelt at Yaergu stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Erhan belonged to the Tong clan; his family had long lived at Yaergu stockade.

sentences.zh: 父扈喇虎，與族人相仇，率所部來歸，是歲​​戊子，。

translations.literal: His father Hulahu feuded with clansmen and led his following to submit; that year was wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hulahu feuded with his clan and brought his people to submit in the wuzi year.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲正白？

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed he was placed in the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the banners were organized he was enrolled in the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵之六年也，扈爾漢年十三，太祖養以為子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year after the Taizu raised his army Hu Erhan was thirteen; the Taizu reared him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the uprising Hu Erhan was thirteen; the Taizu raised him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 稍長，使為侍旗。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was made attendant of the banner.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was made an attendant of the imperial banner.

sentences.zh: 扈爾漢感太祖撫育恩，誓效死，戰輒為前鋒。

translations.literal: Hu Erhan was moved by the Taizu's fostering grace and swore to die in his service; in battle he always served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the Taizu's care, he swore to die in his service and always fought in the van.

sentences.zh: 瓦爾喀部蜚悠城初屬烏喇，貝勒布佔泰待之虐，丁未正月，城長策穆特黑請徙附太祖，太祖命貝勒舒爾哈齊等將三千人迎之，扈爾漢從。

translations.literal: Feiyoucheng in the Warka tribe had first belonged to Ula; Beile Buzhantai treated it harshly. In the first month of the dingwei year its chief Cemutehei asked to move under the Taizu; the Taizu ordered Beile Surhaci and others with three thousand men to welcome them; Hu Erhan followed.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyoucheng in the Warka had lain under Ula until Buzhantai mistreated it. In the first month of dingwei its chief Cemutehei asked to join the Taizu; Surhaci and other beiles went with three thousand men to receive the people, and Hu Erhan marched with them.

sentences.zh: 既至蜚悠城，收環城屯寨凡五百戶，使扈爾漢與揚古利率兵三百，護以前行。

translations.literal: When they reached Feiyoucheng they gathered five hundred households of surrounding stockades and sent Hu Erhan with Yangguli and three hundred men to escort them forward.
translations.idiomatic: At Feiyoucheng they gathered five hundred households from the ring of settlements and sent Hu Erhan with Yangguli and three hundred men to escort them ahead.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰發兵萬人邀諸路，扈爾漢結寨山巔，使蜚悠城之。

translations.literal: Buzhantai sent ten thousand men to block the roads. Hu Erhan fortified a camp on the mountain crest and sent the five hundred households of Feiyoucheng who had come to submit into the stronghold for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhantai threw ten thousand men across the roads. Hu Erhan entrenched on the heights and brought the five hundred Feiyoucheng households who had submitted under the camp's protection.

sentences.zh: 自率二百人與烏喇兵萬人各據山為陣，相持，使馳告後軍，翼日烏喇悉眾來戰，揚古利迎擊，烏喇兵稍退，會後軍至，奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He himself led two hundred men; ten thousand Ula troops each held a mountain and formed battle lines in stalemate. He sent a rider to report to the rear army. The next day Ula came in full force; Yangguli met the attack; Ula troops fell back slightly; when the rear army arrived they charged fiercely and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He kept two hundred men with him while ten thousand Ula soldiers held the hills opposite. He sent word to the rear. Next day the Ula came in full strength; Yangguli met them and forced a pause; when the main body arrived the charge broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，太祖命貝勒巴雅喇將千人伐渥集部，扈爾漢從，取赫席黑俄漠和蘇魯、佛訥赫拕克索三路，俘二千人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer the Taizu ordered Beile Bayara with a thousand men against the Woji tribe; Hu Erhan followed, took the three routes of Hexihei, Emohesulu, and Fonehetuokesuo, and captured two thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Taizu sent Bayara with a thousand men against the Woji; Hu Erhan went along, swept Hexihei, Emohesulu, and Fonehetuokesuo, and brought back two thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 己酉冬十二月，復命扈爾漢將千人伐渥集部，取滹野路，收二千戶以還，太祖嘉其功，賚甲胄及馬，賜號「達爾漢」。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in the year jiyou he was again ordered to lead a thousand men against the Woji tribe, took the Huye route, and brought back two thousand households; the Taizu praised his merit, bestowed armor and horses, and granted the title "Dalahan."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of jiyou he again led a thousand men against the Woji, took the Huye route, and returned with two thousand households. The Taizu rewarded him with armor and horses and gave him the title Dalahan.

sentences.zh: 辛亥冬十二月，復命扈爾漢及何和禮、額亦都將二千人伐渥集部虎爾哈路，克扎庫塔城，斬千餘級，俘二千人；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in the year xinhai he was again ordered with He Heli and E Yidu to lead two thousand men against the Hu'erha route of the Woji tribe; they took Zhakuta city, slew more than a thousand, and captured two thousand;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of xinhai he marched again with He Heli and E Yidu and two thousand men against the Hu'erha route of the Woji; they stormed Zhakuta, killed more than a thousand, and took two thousand prisoners;

sentences.zh: 撫環近諸路，收五百戶以還。

translations.literal: they pacified the neighboring routes and brought back five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: they pacified the nearby routes and escorted five hundred households home.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，太祖討烏喇，扈爾漢及諸將皆從戰，奪門入，遂滅烏喇。

translations.literal: In the year guichou the Taizu campaigned against Ula; Hu Erhan and the other generals all followed in battle, stormed through the gate, and destroyed Ula.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year the Taizu struck Ula; Hu Erhan and the other commanders fought through the gates and brought Ula down.

sentences.zh: 太祖置五大臣，扈爾漢與焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu appointed the Five Great Ministers; Hu Erhan was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Great Ministers were created, Hu Erhan was one of them.

sentences.zh: 先是太祖與明盟，畫界，戒民毋竊逾，違者殺毋赦。

translations.literal: Earlier the Taizu had allied with Ming and drawn a boundary, warning the people not to steal across it; violators were to be killed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Taizu had made peace with the Ming and marked a border, forbidding his people to cross it for plunder on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 至天命初將十年，明民越境採參鑿礦，取樹木果蔬，殆歲有之。

translations.literal: By the tenth year after Tianming was inaugurated, Ming subjects crossed the border to gather ginseng, mine ore, and take timber and fruit—almost every year.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years of Tianming, Ming subjects were crossing yearly to dig ginseng and ore and strip timber and fruit.

sentences.zh: 太祖使扈爾漢行邊，遇明民逾塞，取而殺之，凡五十餘輩。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Hu Erhan to patrol the border; when he met Ming subjects beyond the barrier he seized and killed them—more than fifty parties in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent Hu Erhan to patrol the frontier; whenever he found Ming subjects beyond the barrier he killed them—more than fifty bands in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣綱古里、方吉納如廣寧，廣寧巡撫李維翰系諸獄，而使來責言，且求殺逾塞民者，太祖拒不許。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Ganguli and Fangjina to Guangning; Guangning Grand Coordinator Li Weihan imprisoned them and sent men to rebuke and also demand the killer of those who crossed the barrier; the Taizu refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent Ganguli and Fangjina to Guangning; Grand Coordinator Li Weihan jailed them and demanded the men who had killed border-crossers; the Taizu refused.

sentences.zh: 既乃取葉赫俘十人戮撫順關下，明亦釋使者。

translations.literal: He then took ten Yehe captives and executed them below Fushun Pass; Ming also released the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He then executed ten Yehe prisoners beneath Fushun Pass; the Ming in turn released the envoys.

sentences.zh: 是年秋七月，太祖命扈爾漢及安費揚古將二千人伐薩哈連部，道收兀爾簡河南北三十六寨；

translations.literal: That autumn in the seventh month the Taizu ordered Hu Erhan and Anfiyanggu with two thousand men against the Sahalian tribe; on the way they took thirty-six stockades north and south of the Wuerjian River;
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month the Taizu sent Hu Erhan and Anfiyanggu with two thousand men against Sahalian; en route they reduced thirty-six stockades on both banks of the Wuerjian;

sentences.zh: 遂進攻薩哈連部，取十​​一寨，降其三路。

translations.literal: then advanced against the Sahalian tribe, took eleven stockades, and received the submission of three routes.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed on against Sahalian, took eleven stockades, and received three routes in submission.

sentences.zh: 語詳安費揚古傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Anfiyanggu.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in the biography of Anfiyanggu.

sentences.zh: 四年春二月，明經略楊鎬大舉四道來侵，三月，太祖督軍御之，扈爾漢從貝勒阿敏先行，與明游擊喬一琦遇，擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the fourth year Ming Grand Coordinator Yang Hao came in force on four routes; in the third month the Taizu commanded the army in defense; Hu Erhan followed Beile Amin in advance and met Ming guerrilla Qiao Yiqi, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Yang Hao invaded on four roads; in the third month the Taizu took the field and Hu Erhan marched ahead with Beile Amin, meeting and defeating Ming guerrilla Qiao Yiqi.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮出軍助明，其帥姜弘立屯孤拉庫嶺，一琦收殘卒匿朝鮮營。

translations.literal: At the time Korea sent troops to aid Ming; their commander Jiang Hongli encamped at Gulakuling; Yiqi gathered his broken troops and hid in the Korean camp.
translations.idiomatic: Korea had sent aid to the Ming; Jiang Hongli held Gulakuling while Yiqi hid his survivors in the Korean camp.

sentences.zh: 扈爾漢從諸貝勒擊明軍，戰於薩爾滸，破明將杜松等；

translations.literal: Hu Erhan followed the beiles in striking the Ming army, fought at Sarhu, and broke Ming commanders Du Song and others;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Erhan followed the beiles against the Ming host, fought at Sarhu, and broke Du Song and the other Ming commanders;

sentences.zh: 戰於尚間崖，破明將馬林等：扈爾漢皆在行間。

translations.literal: fought at Shangjianya and broke Ming commanders Ma Lin and others: Hu Erhan was in the ranks throughout.
translations.idiomatic: fought at Shangjianya and broke Ma Lin and the others—Hu Erhan was in the line throughout.

sentences.zh: 明將劉綎自寬奠入董鄂路，牛錄額真托保等戰不利。

translations.literal: The Ming commander Liu Ting entered Dong'e route from Kuandian; niru daikan Tuobao and others fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: Ming commander Liu Ting entered from Kuandian along the Dong'e route; Tuobao and other niru officers fought without success.

sentences.zh: 扈爾漢帥師與托保合軍，憑隘為伏，諸貝勒軍出瓦爾喀什林。

translations.literal: Hu Erhan commanded the army and united with Tuobao; they lay in ambush at a narrow pass while the beiles' army came out through Walikashilin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Erhan united with Tuobao, set an ambush in a defile, while the beiles' main force came through Walikashilin.

sentences.zh: 劉綎將率兵登阿布達里岡為陣，扈爾漢引軍扼其衝，諸貝勒繼至，東西夾擊，破之，綎戰死，明兵遂熸。

translations.literal: Liu Ting was about to lead his troops up Abudali Gang to form battle; Hu Erhan led his army to block the approach; the beiles followed and struck from east and west; they broke him; Ting died in battle and the Ming army was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ting was forming on Abudali Gang when Hu Erhan blocked the approach; the beiles came up on both flanks, shattered his force, and killed Ting on the field until the Ming army was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 五年，太祖取瀋陽，扈爾漢從擊明總兵賀世賢等，敗之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Taizu took Shenyang; Hu Erhan followed in striking Ming commander He Shixian and others and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Shenyang fell; Hu Erhan joined the strike against He Shixian and other Ming commanders and routed them.

sentences.zh: 歷加世職至三等總兵官。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to third-rank commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive honors to third-rank commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 八年冬十月，卒，年甫四十？

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the eighth year he died, having just reached forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the eighth year, only forty years old.

sentences.zh: 八，太祖親臨其喪。

translations.literal: The Taizu came in person to mourn at his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu mourned at his funeral in person.

sentences.zh: 扈爾漢諸子：渾塔襲三等總兵官，其後不著；

translations.literal: Among Hu Erhan's sons: Hunta inherited third-rank commander-in-chief; his later line is not recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Of Hu Erhan's sons, Hunta inherited third-rank commander-in-chief, but the later line is not recorded;

sentences.zh: 準塔別有傳；

translations.literal: Zhunta has a separate biography;
translations.idiomatic: Zhunta has his own biography;

sentences.zh: 阿拉密襲準塔世職，附見準塔傳。

translations.literal: Alami inherited Zhunta's hereditary office, noted in the biography of Zhunta.
translations.idiomatic: Alami succeeded to Zhunta's hereditary post, as noted in Zhunta's biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國初置五大臣以理政聽訟，有征伐則帥師以出，蓋實兼將帥之重焉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the founding of the state the Five Great Ministers were appointed to govern affairs and hear lawsuits; when there was campaigning they led armies forth—thus they truly combined the weight of generalship.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: At the dynasty's founding the Five Great Ministers governed and judged suits, and led armies when war came—they truly united civil rule with command of the field.

sentences.zh: 額亦都歸太祖最早，巍然元從，戰閥亦最多。

translations.literal: E Yidu submitted to the Taizu earliest, stood as the founding pillar among the first followers, and his battle record is also the longest.
translations.idiomatic: E Yidu came to the Taizu before any other, stood as a founding pillar of the first companions, and left the longest record of battles.

sentences.zh: 費英東尤以忠讜著，歷朝褒許，稱佐命第一。

translations.literal: Fei Yingdong was especially noted for loyal bluntness; successive courts praised him as the foremost founding assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yingdong was famed above all for blunt loyalty; every reign called him the first of the founding assistants.

sentences.zh: 何和禮、安費揚古、扈爾漢後先奔走，共成篳路藍縷之烈，積三十年，輔成大業，功施爛然。

translations.literal: He Heli, Anfiyanggu, and Hu Erhan ran to and fro in turn, together accomplishing the hardship of beginning in poverty; through thirty years they aided the great enterprise until their merit blazed bright.
translations.idiomatic: He Heli, Anfiyanggu, and Hu Erhan served in turn through thirty years of hardship, building the enterprise until their deeds shone together.

sentences.zh: 太祖建號後，諸子皆長且才，故五大臣沒而四大貝勒執政。

translations.literal: After the Taizu established his title his sons were all grown and capable; therefore when the Five Great Ministers died the Four Great Beiles took government.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Taizu had proclaimed his state his sons were grown and able; when the Five Great Ministers were gone the Four Great Beiles ruled in their place.

sentences.zh: 他塔喇希福祖羅屯，傳言列五大臣，或初闕員時嘗簡補歟？

translations.literal: Tatara Xifu's ancestor Luotun is said in tradition to have been listed among the Five Great Ministers—perhaps he was chosen to fill an early vacancy?
translations.idiomatic: Tradition names Luotun, ancestor of Tatara Xifu, among the Five Great Ministers—perhaps a seat was filled when one was first left empty?

sentences.zh: 草昧傳聞，蓋不可深考矣。

translations.literal: Such tales from the age of obscurity cannot be examined deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Such rumors from the founding days cannot be traced with certainty.
